title: Germany presses Moscow and Kyiv to end the Russian gas crisis.
text: The Russia–Ukraine gas disputes refer to a number of disputes between Ukrainian oil and gas company Naftogaz Ukrayiny and Russian gas supplier Gazprom over natural gas supplies, prices, and debts. title: 5–15 February – 59th Berlin International Film Festival
text: The 59th Berlin International Film Festival was held from 5 February to 15 February 2009. The opening film of the festival was Tom Tykwer’s The International, screened out of competition.

title: Germany in the Eurovision Song Contest 2009
text: Germany was represented at the Eurovision Song Contest 2009 with the song "Miss Kiss Kiss Bang", written by Alex Christensen and Steffen Häfelinger, and performed by Alex Swings Oscar Sings!, consisting of producer Alex Christensen and singer Oscar Loya. The German participating broadcaster on behalf of ARD, Norddeutscher Rundfunk, internally selected its entry for the contest.
wiki: Germany in the Eurovision Song Contest 2009

title: The Volkswagen Polo Mk5 is launched at the Geneva Motor Show and was voted European Car of the Year eight months later.
text: The Volkswagen Polo Mk5 is the fifth generation of the Polo, a supermini-class car manufactured by Volkswagen since 2009. The vehicle unveiled at the 2009 Geneva Motor Show in March 2009, while the three-door version was unveiled at the 2009 Frankfurt Motor Show in September 2009.

title: A 17-year-old former student goes on a rampage at his former school in Winnenden, Germany, killing at least fifteen people, before turning the gun on himself.
text: On 11 March 2009, a series of shootings took place at the Albertville-Realschule in Winnenden and a car dealership in Wendlingen, Baden-Württemberg, Germany. Fifteen people were killed and nine were injured before the perpetrator, 17-year-old former student Tim Kretschmer, killed himself during a shootout with police.

title: 2009 German presidential election
text: An indirect presidential election was held in Germany on 23 May 2009. The president of Germany is elected by the Federal Convention, which is made up of the members of the Bundestag and an equal number of members elected by the state parliaments.

title: 15–23 August – 2009 World Championships in Athletics takes place in Berlin. Usain Bolt breaks the world records for 200 metres and 100 metres.
text: Usain St. Leo Bolt is a Jamaican retired sprinter.

title: 2009 Saarland state election, 2009 Saxony state election and 2009 Thuringia state election take place
text: The 2009 Saarland state election was held on 30 August 2009 to elect the members of the Landtag of Saarland. It was held on the same day as state elections in Saxony and Thuringia.

title: Opel launches new Astra at Frankfurt Motor Show.
text: The Opel Astra is a compact car/small family car developed and produced by the German automaker Opel since 1991, currently at its sixth generation. It was first launched in September 1991 as a direct replacement to the Opel Kadett.

title: 2009 German federal election takes place. Angela Merkel wins reelection as chancellor.
text: A federal election was held in Germany on 27 September 2009 to elect the members of the 17th Bundestag. The Christian Democratic Union, its Bavarian sister party, the Christian Social Union (CSU), and the Free Democratic Party (FDP) won the election, and the three parties formed a new centre-right government with Angela Merkel as chancellor.

title: 2009 Schleswig-Holstein state election and 2009 Brandenburg state election take place.
text: The 2009 Schleswig-Holstein state election was held on 27 September 2009 to elect the members of the Landtag of Schleswig-Holstein. It was held on the same day as the 2009 federal election and the 2009 Brandenburg state election.

title: German bishop Margot Käßmann becomes first elected woman as leader of Evangelical Church in Germany.
text: Margot Käßmann is a Lutheran theologian, who was Landesbischöfin (bishop) of the Evangelical-Lutheran Church of Hanover in Germany. On 28 October 2009, she was also elected to lead the Protestant Church in Germany, a federation of Protestant church bodies in Germany.

title: The Second Merkel cabinet led by Angela Merkel was sworn in.
text: The Second Merkel cabinet was the Government of the Federal Republic of Germany during the 17th legislative session of the Bundestag. Installed after the 2009 federal election, it left office on 17 December 2013.

title: Christine Lieberknecht (CDU) becomes Minister-President of state Thuringia.
text: Christine Lieberknecht is a German politician of the Christian Democratic Union (CDU). From 2009 to 2014, she served as the Minister President of Thuringia.

title: Wolfgang Schneiderhan, the Chief of Staff of the German Bundeswehr, and Franz Josef Jung resign over allegations that they withheld information in the aftermath of the Kunduz airstrike.
text: Wolfgang Schneiderhan is a German general who served as Inspector General of the Bundeswehr from 2002 to 2009.

title: Ursula von der Leyen becomes Federal Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs (Germany) and Kristina Köhler becomes new Federal Ministry of Family Affairs, Senior Citizens, Women and Youth
text: Ursula Gertrud von der Leyen is a German politician and physician who has served as President of the European Commission since 2019. She served in the German federal government between 2005 and 2019, holding positions in Angela Merkel's cabinet, most recently as Federal Minister for Defence.

title: Dresdner Bank was acquired by German Commerzbank.
text: Dresdner Bank AG was a German bank, founded in 1872 in Dresden, then headquartered in Berlin from 1884 to 1945 and in Frankfurt from 1963 onwards after a postwar hiatus. Long Germany's second-largest bank behind Deutsche Bank, it was eventually acquired by Commerzbank in May 2009.

title: “Hot n Cold” by Katy Perry
text: "Hot n Cold" is a song by American singer Katy Perry from her second studio album, One of the Boys. She and Max Martin co-wrote the song with its producer Dr.

title: “Broken Strings” by 2009-01-30 30 January
text: "Broken Strings" is the second single by British musician James Morrison from his second studio album, Songs for You, Truths for Me, and was released in December 2008. The song is a duet with Canadian singer-songwriter Nelly Furtado.

title: “Irgendwas bleibt” by Silbermond
text: Silbermond is a German pop rock band from Bautzen, Saxony. The band consists of Stefanie Kloß, Andreas Nowak, and brothers Johannes and Thomas Stolle.

title: “Poker Face” by Lady Gaga
text: "Poker Face" is a song by American singer Lady Gaga from her debut studio album, The Fame. The track was released on September 23, 2008, as the album's second single, through Streamline Records, KonLive, Cherrytree Records, and Interscope Records.

title: “Anything but Love” by Daniel Schuhmacher
text: "Anything but Love" is a song by German recording artist Daniel Schuhmacher, the winner of the sixth season of the television competition Deutschland sucht den Superstar. Written and produced by DSDS judge Dieter Bohlen, it was released as both his coronation song and debut single.

title: “Jungle Drum” by Emilíana Torrini
text: "Jungle Drum" is the third single released from Icelandic singer-songwriter Emilíana Torrini's third studio album, Me and Armini. It was released as a digital download on 9 March 2009 and later on 19 June 2009 as a CD single in Germany.

title: “If a Song Could Get Me You” by Marit Larsen
text: "If a Song Could Get Me You" is a single by Norwegian singer-songwriter Marit Larsen. It served as Larsen's first international single and reached No.

title: “Pussy” by Rammstein
text: "Pussy" is a song by German Neue Deutsche Härte band Rammstein. It was released as the lead single from the band's sixth studio album, Liebe ist für alle da on 18 September 2009.

title: “Sexy Bitch” by 2009-10-09 9 October
text: "Sexy Bitch" is a song by French DJ David Guetta from his fourth studio album One Love (2009). The song features vocals from Senegalese-American singer Akon.

title: “Paparazzi” by Lady Gaga
text: "Paparazzi" is a song by American singer Lady Gaga from her debut studio album, The Fame. It was released by Interscope Records as the fifth and final single from the album.

title: “Bodies” by Robbie Williams
text: "Bodies" is a song by English recording artist Robbie Williams. It was released on 12 October 2009 by EMI as the lead single from his eighth studio album, Reality Killed the Video Star.

title: “Pflaster” by Ich + Ich
text: Ich + Ich is a musical project by German musicians Annette Humpe and Adel Tawil.

title: “Meet Me Halfway” by 2009-12-11 11 December
text: "Meet Me Halfway" is the third single from the Black Eyed Peas' fifth studio album, The E.N.D.. Released in September 2009, the song peaked at number seven on the US Billboard Hot 100 and topped the charts of Australia, Germany, Romania, Mexico, and the United Kingdom where "Meet Me Halfway" became the 10th-biggest-selling single of 2009.

title: “I Will Love You Monday (365)” by 2009-12-18 18 December
text: "I Will Love You Monday" is a song by Danish singer-songwriter Aura Dione from her debut album Columbine. It was released as her debut single in Europe on 10 November 2009 by Island Records, except Denmark, where the original version, "I Will Love You Monday", was released as her third single in August 2008.

title: “I Like” by 2009-12-25 25 December
text: "I Like" is a song by American singer Keri Hilson. It was written and produced by German musicians David Jost and Robin Grubert and recorded by Hilson for the soundtrack for the German film Zweiohrküken.
